newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to ask experts to sort out European company impasse.
newsitem.headline: EU to ask experts to sort out European company impasse.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it would ask a group of experts to try to resolve a longstanding impasse over legislation that would allow firms to set up as "European" companies rather than national ones.
The question has stymied European Union governments, which have been discussing the idea of a European Company Statute for more than 20 years.

The main conflict has involved provisions on worker participation in company decisions, with Germany promoting its own system of "co-determination" between employees and managers and Britain arguing there should be no mandatory rules.
Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn told reporters after a meeting of EU social affairs ministers that he would ask five "high-level" labour policy experts to tackle the problem.
He also confirmed that he planned to ask trade unions and employers to negotiate rules to require national companies to set up procedures to inform and consult their workers.
That accord could then be turned into EU law.

The initiative -- which would be taken under the Social Protocol, which exempts Britain -- would complement the EU's "works council directive", which already requires multinational companies to set up such systems.

The social affairs ministers generally supported the idea of setting up a committee to examine the European Company Statute, although Britain questioned whether it would achieve anything, EU officials said.

The Union is coming under increasing pressure from industry to close what is seen as a big gap in its effort to create a single market -- the inability of companies with operations in different member states to form a single legal entity under EU law.

But Germany has insisted on requiring European companies to set up procedures equivalent to its own system of employee representation on company boards. It rejected a recent Commission proposal to draw up EU-wide legislation on worker consultation that would apply to the new European companies, saying that fell short of worker "participation".

Flynn said he would appoint the experts -- including representatives of the European Trade Union Confederation and the Union of Industrial and Employers' Confederations of Europe -- by the end of the year and ask them to report back in three months.

He said their effort could also unblock legislation that would create legal frameworks for a European association, European cooperative society and European mutual society, all of which are also blocked by the worker-participation dispute.
